method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill, from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; a seat-neutral core (maca-core.l4, with four regulative rules: ss 7(3), 31, 31A and the review chain of ss 28A, 28B, 28E) and two seat layers that restate no rule (maca-seat.l4 for the person injured, maca-seat-survivors.l4 for those left after a death); no REFUSE (an accident before the amendments now in force, a part week, or an impairment percentage between the rows of the s 17(2) table answers `outside this encoding`, asserted); checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Act: reprint REPM022, as in force at 31 May 2019 (last amendment Act No. 18 of 2019, commenced 31 May 2019), deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/Motor-Accidents-Compensation-Act-1979-NT-current-reprint-REPM022.txt; later amendments to the Act may be missing. Regulations: reprint REPM022R1, as in force at 28 August 2026, deposited at ../../../motor-accidents-compensation-regulations-1984/registers/source-bundle/Motor-Accidents-Compensation-Regulations-1984-NT-current-reprint-REPM022R1.txt

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run maca-core.l4 ; l4 run maca-seat.l4 ; l4 run maca-seat-survivors.l4 ; l4 run maca-cases-injured.l4 ; l4 run maca-cases-survivors.l4
checks.result: 234 assertions satisfied (162 in maca-cases-injured.l4, 72 in maca-cases-survivors.l4, of which 5 mirror cases), 0 errors, 0 warnings (2026-10-24); 7 #TRACEs with an expect line (3 breaches by the claimant, 3 obligations pending, 1 late request leaving nothing owed), each read and as expected
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read.

scope: In: ss 4 (definitions), 4A, 4B, 4C with reg 4 (AMA Guides 6th edition, a fact), 4DA (as facts); s 7; s 9 with reg 4A, ss 9A-9G with reg 4B (a fact), ss 10, 10A-10C, 11, 11A, 11B; s 13(1), (2), (2A), (3) (the amount an input: the formula was lost in conversion), (5), (5A); s 14; s 17; s 18 with reg 4D (whether a service is covered); ss 18BA-18BE with regs 4E, 4F (eligibility only); ss 20, 20A with reg 4M, ss 21-24, 37; s 25 with regs 5, 6; ss 31, 31A, 28A, 28B, 28E; ss 46, 47, 49 as the limits of the encoding. Out: Part 2, s 12, s 13(4), (6), ss 18A, 18B (pre-2014 attendant care), reg 4G and Schedule 2, reg 4J, s 18C, s 19 with regs 4K, 4L, s 28D, ss 29-30C, ss 32-35, s 38, s 40, Part 8, the commuted amount. Read with subjects/au/social-security-act-1991 (pension age, s 23; compensation recovery, ss 17, 1166-1173), subjects/au/income-tax-assessment-act-1997 (tax treatment of the weekly compensation), subjects/au/nt/return-to-work-act-1986 (s 10A input; RTW ss 4(2A), 61(2)) and subjects/au/nt/victims-of-crime-assistance-act-2006 (its s 17 excludes an injury entitled to benefits here); cross-folder IMPORT is not possible.
seats: the person injured in a motor accident (the eligible person, and the claimant)
on a death: the spouse, a dependent child, a dependent parent, and the person liable to meet the expense of the funeral
